segments.text: To fully grasp HTML, it's crucial to visualize its hierarchical structure. At the very top, we declare `<!DOCTYPE html>`, which informs the browser about the document type. This isn't an HTML tag itself, but an instruction.
The actual root element for all HTML content is the `<html>` tag. Inside this `<html>` tag, we find two primary children: the `<head>` and the `<body>`.

The `<head>` section contains all the invisible metadata about your page—things like the page title that appears in the browser tab, character set information, and links to external CSS files. Crucially, the content within `<head>` is not directly displayed on the webpage.

In contrast, the `` section is where all your visible content resides. This includes everything from your main headings defined by `

Each of these elements can be nested within others, creating a clear, logical tree-like structure that browsers interpret to render your webpage. Understanding this nested hierarchy is key to writing well-formed and predictable HTML.
